criterion_notes.c1: Examines clean drinking water supply service in the Pemalang City area served by the Regional Public Drinking Water Company (Perumda Tirta Mulia), reporting household connections (40,074 SR in the city service area; 56,201 SR regency-wide), administrative service coverage (12.74%), technical service coverage (18.50%), and service duration (22 to 24 hours).
criterion_notes.c2: Fails under BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain wording, this is a pure civil/environmental engineering evaluation of raw water discharge, reservoir capacity, pipeline hydraulics (using EPANET 2.0), and geometric water demand projections; ministerial regulations (e.g., Regulation of the Minister of Public Works No. 18/2007 and No. 27/2016, Permenkes No. 32/2017) and BPKP audit figures are cited solely as technical engineering design benchmarks and baseline operational statistics, not analyzed as legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factors. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, no rule-type mechanism governing service access (eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure effects on access) is studied.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains empirical operational data from the 2020 BPKP audit and utility records, field observations/interviews, raw water quality test results, and EPANET 2.0 hydraulic modeling of the existing pipeline network.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports descriptive outcomes relevant to access and service continuity, including administrative service coverage (12.74%), technical service coverage (18.50%), number of house connections (40,074 SR), service duration (22 to 24 hours), network pressure, and projected supply adequacy up to 2030.
criterion_notes.c5: Population/service area (Pemalang, Taman, and Bantarbolang sub-districts; 479,856 residents; 40,074 house connections) and engineering performance metrics are identifiable, along with a descriptive engineering evaluation design, but there is no identifiable legal, administrative, or governance exposure variable linked to service access.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: The service coverage of Pemalang Regency Drinking Water Perumda in 2020 is still low, namely the administrative service coverage of 12.74% and the technical service coverage of 18.50%

Evaluation of the drinking water supply system in the Pemalang City area includes several things, including raw water units, production units, distribution units, service units, and the influencing factors as the basis for further development planning.

Schematic analysis of the piping network with the help of the EPANET 2.0 program. The program is a computer program (software) with a Windows interface that can perform single or multiple-period simulations of hydraulic behavior and water quality in pressurized pipelines.
The duration of drinking water service ranges from 22 hours to 24 hours. The absence of a zone system also causes the water not to be distributed evenly.

Currently, the installed capacity is 600 liters/second, so based on the calculation table above for the average water demand, the installed capacity is still capable of supplying up to 2025, but for water needs at peak hours, the installed capacity is only able to supply until 2022.

raw_response.exposure: Technical infrastructure capacity and hydraulic network characteristics (raw water discharge, reservoir volume, transmission and distribution pipeline head/pressure); no legal, administrative, or governance exposure examined
raw_response.outcome: Administrative service coverage (12.74%), technical service coverage (18.50%), house connections (40,074 SR), service duration (22 to 24 hours), leakage rate (26.93%), node pressures, and projected raw water supply adequacy through 2030
raw_response.population_and_sample: Clean water supply system (SPAM) of Perumda Tirta Mulia in the Pemalang City area (Pemalang, Taman, and Bantarbolang sub-districts; 479,856 residents and 40,074 house connections in 2020)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E06 (Engineering only). Although the paper reports descriptive utility coverage (12.74% administrative coverage; 40,074 house connections) and service duration (22–24 hours) for Pemalang Regency's water utility, the study is a pure hydraulic and water-supply engineering evaluation examining spring discharge capacity, reservoir volume, EPANET 2.0 pipeline pressure/headloss simulations, and geometric population/water demand projections to 2030. Ministerial regulations are referenced only as technical engineering design standards (e.g., leakage thresholds, 24-hour flow criteria, 100 L/person/day demand assumption), so the study fails Criterion 2 under both the plain wording and the 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading.
raw_response.study_design: Descriptive engineering system evaluation, EPANET 2.0 hydraulic simulation, and geometric water demand projection
